pages.title: Straight-Tusked Elephant
pages.text: The straight-tusked elephant ($(o)Palaeoloxodon antiquus$()) is an extinct elephant that lived in Europe and western Asia during the Middle and Late Pleistocene.$(br2)It was one of the largest land mammals of the Pleistocene, with large males standing around four metres at the shoulder, and was named for its long, only gently curved tusks.$(br2)It thrived in warm temperate forests during the interglacial periods, browsing on trees and shrubs.
